subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.

spec.name: Warhound 2077 Militarized Truck
spec.description: A heavy low-poly cyberpunk 6x6 armored military truck with an angular armored cab, a cargo bed with a rocket-launcher turret, neon trim and big chunky wheels.
spec.layout: A long, low, wedge-shaped armored truck facing +Z. Front: sloped armored hood with a bull-bar, a wide LED headlight strip and winch bumper. Cab sits just behind the hood at z 1.6..3.0 with a raked angular windshield (glowing cyan slit glass), side armor plates and roof light bar. Behind the cab runs a flat cargo deck with armored side panels, a pintle-mounted roof-of-bed turret near z -1.6 and a rear ramp/exhaust cluster at the back. Three axles (front z=2.9, mid z=-0.7, rear z=-2.7) with six chunky wheels (radius 0.62) under wide wheel arches. Everything is faceted and boxy with chamfered plates, yellow hazard trim, cyan and magenta neon strips along the skirts, and panelled/riveted dark metal paints, decals and glyph textures. Chassis and wheels rest on the floor; the cab, bed and turret sit above on the frame.

parts.builds: The load-bearing frame and body underside: two long ladder rails, cross members, skirt armor panels with neon cyan and magenta strips glowing along the lower edges, wheel arches with hazard-yellow trim, three axle housings with differential pumpkins and drive shafts, suspension springs (coil) and shock absorbers, fuel and battery tanks slung between axles, underbody plating with panelled riveted paint, fender flares over all six wheels, front bumper with winch, bull-bar, tow hooks, and headlight/lamp pods (glow). Includes a long sloped armored hood (engine cover) from z 3.0 to 4.0 with vents, grille glyph texture and a roof-ridge, plus front lamp strip.
parts.attaches: Root of the body joint at frameTop. Cab starts at cabFloor; bed deck starts at bedDeck; wheels hang on frontAxle, midAxle, rearAxle; rear bumper at rearBumper; front bumper at bumperFront.

parts.builds: Six chunky low-poly wheels (radius 0.62, width 0.5) as separate parts on wheelFL..wheelRR: faceted 12-sided tires with tread blocks ringed around, rim discs with bolt rings (8 lug nuts), hub caps with a glowing cyan ring or glyph decal, brake discs with drilled holes and calipers in warnRed, mud flaps with decal. Wheel centre heights 0.62 so tires touch y=0. Spokes/rim paint metal-like with grunge dark at the edges.
parts.attaches: Rides the wheel joints at the axle mounts; sits inside chassis fender arches (x from 1.05 to 1.55 each side).

parts.builds: The armored crew cab from z 0.6 to 3.0, floor at cabFloor (y 1.3) up to y 2.9: faceted wedge shell with sloped raked windshield and side windows in dark glass with glowing cyan HUD-like SVG textures and thin armored slits, thick pillar frames, side armor plates with hazard stripe decals and unit emblem decal (angular wolf-head sigil), door seams with handles, side mirrors with camera pods, roof sensor mast, antenna array, roof-mounted light bar (glowing white/magenta), roof hatch, rivets via panelled paint, interior seats and a dashboard with screens glowing (visible through the glass), exhaust stacks behind the cab (two vertical stacks with heat-glow caps) at z 0.5.
parts.attaches: Sits on the chassis at cabFloor; back wall meets bed at cabBack (z 0.6); front meets the hood at z 3.0.

parts.builds: The cargo bed from z 0.5 down to -4.0 at deck height bedDeck (y 1.45): armored deck plate with grip-pattern paint, side walls with angled armor panels, cargo ribs, hazard stripes, stencilled serial text decals, tie-down rings, a cargo load of sealed crates and fuel barrels (olive with trim stencils and glowing status lights), a tool rack, tail lights (red glow), the rear drop ramp panel on the rampHinge joint with yellow chevrons, a rear bumper with tow hitch, twin exhaust pipes, fuel filler cap, plus a ring-mount base (rotating track ring with teeth) at turretRing for the turret, and a roll cage hoop behind the cab with a spotlight.
parts.attaches: Rests on the chassis at bedDeck; turret base ring meets the turret at turretRing; ramp hinges at rampHinge; front wall meets cab back at cabBack.

parts.builds: The remote weapon station on the turretRing mount (0,2.0,-1.6): a rotating pedestal on turretYaw with a faceted armored housing, a cradle on turretPitch carrying a heavy twin autocannon with perforated barrel shrouds, muzzle brakes, ammo belt feeds and an ammo box, plus a side pod of 6 rocket tubes (2x3) with warhead cones in warnRed, sensor head with a glowing cyan lens (decal reticle) and a laser rangefinder, antenna whip, hazard-yellow trim, kill-mark decals and rivet panelling, and small glowing status LEDs. Barrels point +Z in rest pose, length about 1.6 m.
parts.attaches: Base sits on the bed's ring mount at turretRing; yaw joint turretYaw at turretRing, pitch joint turretPitch above it.

calls.reasoning:
I'm planning a buildCab function that constructs the cab geometry using box parts anchored to the cab joint, with coordinates for the main body and a wedge-shaped shell section.

For the shell, I'm defining a side profile outline in z-y space (rear bottom, front bottom, hood, windshield rake, roof, rear) and extruding it along x to form the cab's silhouette, applying a panelled armor texture, then separately adding a windshield plane angled to match the hood-to-roof slope.

Now I'm positioning the windshield plane with an outward-tilted normal and lifting it slightly off the shell surface, sizing it to fit within the shell's width, and applying a glowing HUD texture. I'm also placing side window planes on the left and right faces of the cab at a fixed height and depth.

Then I'm adding front and rear side windows, frame pillars, armor plates with hazard-stripe decals, door emblems and seams, mirrors with camera pods, a roof light bar with antennas and a hatch, and interior seat/dashboard geometry visible behind the glass.

Adjusting exhaust stack placement so they don't intrude into the bed, tightening radius and position relative to the cab wall. I'm planning the texture set (HUD, hazard, wolf decal, glass panels) and how glow effects apply to textured versus plain parts, plus adding cyan neon strips along the cab base and a raised roof ridge plate for detail.

Now I'm sketching helper functions for creating boxes with position, color, and bone attachments, and setting up mirrored side-panel placements so decals read correctly from outside the vehicle. I'm also working out the hazard stripe texture placement along the lower door skirt area.

I'm figuring out exact placement for door details—armor plate boxes, emblem decals, and door seams—nudging the z-coordinates so the emblem sits centered between seams and the handle doesn't overlap the armor plate.

I'll add a small handle box near the window level, import the glow module from the kit without typing Ctx explicitly, and design the windshield texture as a dark panel with cyan HUD line accents instead of leaving it transparent. Now I'm ready to write the actual code.

I'm planning the buildWheels function using the Ctx context object, placing each wheel joint at its center with the bone axis aligned along x and cylinder geometry oriented along y.

For the tire itself, I'm sizing a 12-sided cylinder carefully, compensating for the faceting so flat faces and vertices stay within the wheel box, then layering small tread blocks around the rim radius to form the tire's texture without exceeding the outer bounds.

Defining tread block geometry...

Rather than using ring items for tread blocks, I realize it's simpler to build the merged tread geometry myself in the wheel's local frame, positioning each block by angle and rotating boxes around the cylinder axis, then merging all blocks into one geometry before placing with a single part call oriented by direction vector—keeping both wheel sides symmetric.

Now I'm planning out the rest of the wheel assembly: rim disc, merged lug nuts, hub cap, a glowing ring accent, brake disc, caliper, and mud flap, all positioned relative to the wheel center at x=±1.3 with proper outward-facing offsets so the brake disc sits recessed inside the rim.

I'm thinking instead of hiding the brake disc, I could build the rim with a dark recessed well disc and a steel brake disc layered on top, using a drilled-hole texture mapped onto the cylinder's top cap to simulate the cutouts rather than modeling actual holes.

Adding more wheel details...

Now I'm planning mud flaps behind each wheel - thin flat boxes positioned outward and low, mounted behind the wheel wells.

I'll texture the mud flap box faces with a hazard/skull graphic in dark rubber tones with yellow chevrons, keeping it to six flaps total on the mid wheels. For tire paint, I'm mixing a grunge noise pattern between the tire color and dark edges, adding a brownish tint near the bottom for mud buildup.

For sidewall detail, I'll add a thin yellow trim ring using a lathe geometry outline positioned near the tire's outer edge, skipping any text decals to keep things simple.

Counting parts per wheel, I land around 11-12 components covering tire, treads, rim lip, spokes, brake disc, caliper, hubcap, glowing ring and lugs, pushing the total part count toward roughly 84 once duplicated across wheels. For colors, I'm settling on a limited palette reusing the tire, hull, rim, trim, neon cyan and warning red tones, with a noise-mixed metal paint for the rim surface.

Working out the grunge effect by computing radial distance from each wheel's axis and darkening based on noise and distance, then placing a glowing cyan hex decal on a textured plane mounted to each wheel bone. I'm sketching the wheel mount positions along the chassis (front, mid, rear) and planning a geometry helper that rotates and translates box/cylinder pieces into a circular tread arrangement before merging them into one mesh.

Still working through tire block placement...

I'm working out how to define the buildBed function signature, keeping the Ctx type as provided by the module rather than importing it separately, then planning out the bed's constituent elements.

Laying out dimensions and positions for the deck, ramp hinge, side walls, and ribbed armor panels, then deciding on paints, textures like hazard stripes and serial numbers, and helper functions for boxes and glow effects.

I'm placing crates with stencils, barrel props, tool racks, tail lights, rear bumper, hitch, and twin exhaust pipes, working out their exact coordinates relative to the vehicle body.

Now I'm designing the turret ring assembly: a pedestal base cylinder, a lathed ring with teeth sitting on top, and making sure the crate and barrel placements avoid overlapping the ring's footprint near the rear of the deck.

Behind the cab I'm adding a roll cage hoop made of rod sweeps forming an arc, plus a spotlight with a glowing lens mounted on top. For construction I'm setting up a cylinder helper aligned along a given axis direction, using degree-based rotations for boxes, and placing around sixteen to eighteen small teeth boxes evenly around the ring's circumference.

I'm also planning hazard-stripe diagonal SVG textures on the outward-facing wall rim panels, stenciled serial text like "WH-2077 // CARGO-7" in white with a transparent background, and panelled armor-colored wall surfaces sized to 0.4 units.

Now I'm adding yellow chevron SVG decals on the ramp's rear face, positioning the ramp geometry attached to the rampHinge bone, and placing glowing red tail lights near the rear corner posts around x=±1.3.

I'm also adding small tie-down ring toruses at six deck spots, rib strips on the deck surface, a cyan neon glow strip along the bed's bottom edges, and building a crate helper function to generate stacked cargo crates with edge straps, stencil decals, and status LEDs alongside barrels.

I need to plan the turret function carefully, mapping out the joint hierarchy for turretYaw and turretPitch with their positions and orientations, deciding how gun parts should attach relative to the pitch bone's coordinate space.

Working out the turret geometry: a faceted octagonal housing, trunnion yoke arms extending from the sides, and barrel dimensions sized to fit within the pitch pivot's range so the gun cradle sits correctly on the yaw ring base.

Now I'm detailing the twin-barrel assembly — shroud cylinders with perforation patterns, muzzle brakes with dark slits, and bore cutouts at the tips — plus sketching out side rocket pods arranged in a grid pattern.

Adding warhead cones rotated to point forward from the tube fronts, plus a dark pod box behind spanning the tube bank, with tube openings suggested as darker rings at the front face.

Next I'm adding an asymmetric ammo box on the right side with an olive trim stripe, plus a brass belt-feed sweep linking it to the gun body, checking the box stays within bounds and rides with the pitch bone. I'm also starting a sensor head mounted on top of the housing.

Adding a red LED tip to the whip antenna and planning hazard stripe decals using textured planes on the housing, plus kill-mark tally decals positioned on the cylindrical housing's flat sides.

I notice the pod geometry slightly overlaps the housing edge, so I'm raising the pod center up with tubes repositioned, adjusting the box top, and recentering the gun, cheeks, cradle, and ammo box around y 2.7-2.8 for better clearance.

Checking the housing's z-extent against the rear bustle box placement to avoid collisions, keeping the box panelled rather than textured. I'm also planning small glowing status LED boxes on the housing top and head using the glow kit for cyan, magenta, red, and green accents.

For the hull, I'm layering a mottled paint blend between hull and armor palette colors wrapped in a panelled texture for a weathered metal look, keeping flat colors limited to just a handful from the palette. I'm also sketching out simple SVG assets for hazard stripes and a crosshair reticle to use as surface decals.

Now I'm detailing the ring base and collar geometry near the bed mount, adding a skirt ring and bolt loops around a 12-sided cylinder to give it a mechanical, riveted look.

For the shroud perforations, I'm working out a loop to place small dark boxes in rings around each barrel, then merging all those duplicated geometries into a single buffer to keep part count manageable instead of spawning dozens of individual meshes.

Now I'm designing the muzzle brake as a small dark box at the barrel tip with side slits, plus figuring out the barrel's internal structure: bare rod radius, shroud length, and brake position layered along the z-axis so everything lines up correctly.

Adjusting barrel segment boundaries, then planning the ammo belt feed: I'll generate a curved path from the ammo box to the receiver and place brass link boxes along it using an "along" helper bound to the turret pitch bone.

For the gun mantlet shield, I'm sketching a tilted plate in front of the cradle with a slight rotation, plus a hazard-stripe texture plane mounted flush on its front face.

Shrinking mantlet width to 0.66 so it clears the cheek plates, and checking that cheek, cradle receiver, pod, and ammo box x-ranges don't collide. Now I'm roughing out a rangefinder as a pair of cylinders along the sensor head sides.

Placing the laser emitter and receiver lenses with red/cyan glow, building the sensor head pedestal, box, front lens cylinder, and reticle plane, then adding top-mounted rangefinder cylinders and verifying the pod and sensor positions stay within the housing bounds.

I'm attaching the gun to the pitch bone and the sensor head to the yaw bone, then adding alternating-colored LED boxes on the rear bustle, rivet spheres ringing the top deck, tally-mark kill markings, and hazard-stripe trim plates plus a yellow trim ring around the housing.

For the housing, I'm positioning the cylinder on the yaw bone with a collar and ring sized to fit within the body width, then adding an antenna whip that curves upward from the top deck with a tapered radius and a glowing red tip LED. Now I'm writing helper functions for adding parts and building box and cylinder geometries...

Still writing helper functions...

I'm darkening the pod tube interior, adding a thin hazard trim on the frame, and attaching a rear bracket arm connecting to the cheek piece.

I'm planning a compact chassis-building function using box and sweep helpers for coils, with a glow-kit effect and clockwork-style metal paneling, keeping the geometry calls simple to avoid API errors.

Now I'm working out the actual layout: positioning the frame, wheel wells, and skirt panels so they clear the wheels without colliding, calculating z-ranges for front/mid/rear wheels and spacing skirt segments between them. I'm sketching fender flares as simple boxes above each wheel arch with trim strips, trying to keep the geometry simple while avoiding overlap with the cab floor and body width.

I'm placing the chassis rails, cross members, and underbody plate at heights that avoid colliding with the axle housings, then adding axle rods, a differential pumpkin sphere, and a drive shaft connecting the two axles. I'm starting to plan coil springs using a sweep helper between the axle and frame.

Now I'm thinking through shocks, fuel tank, and battery box placement, making sure the tank cylinder at x .7 doesn't overlap the wheels sitting further out at x≥1.05.

Shifting to the hood and cab area, I'm sketching a sloped side-profile outline running along z with the chassis capped at y 1.6, trying to get the front hood taper and windshield slope to read correctly before extruding.

Adding dark vent slats on top, placing a grille glyph on the front face, and positioning the front bumper box, though I need to fix the z-limit conflict on the bumper geometry.

Still placing bumper components...

Now adding tow hooks and yellow wheel arch trim strips along the flare edges, considering a simple arc sweep for tube-like trim around each wheel.

That confirms the +180 sweep ends at the top, so I'll place yellow arch sweeps at both inner and outer x positions per wheel, giving 12 sweeps total with the tops reaching y 1.34. I'm also considering a fender flare slab covering the top of the wheel and skipping the wheel-well liner detail to keep things simple.

For the skirts, I'm adding alternating cyan and magenta neon strips along the outer faces at specific heights, plus hazard-stripe texture planes positioned at the skirt's top rim using an SVG diagonal pattern. I'm breaking the skirt into segments around the wheels, accounting for fender coverage near the mid-axle area and adding another segment behind the rear wheel.

I'm deciding to skip the complex chamfer geometry and instead just stack a plate, neon strip, hazard decal, and rivet-line box for simplicity, then move on to designing the rear crossmember near the back of the chassis.

Now I'm sketching hood vent slats as small dark boxes along the flat top of the hood with a cyan glow strip beneath them, plus a raised center ridge running along the hood's length for detail.

Then I work out the sloped hood-to-nose polygon, defining front face points so the shape tapers cleanly into the bumper without self-intersecting edges, before placing the grille as a flat plane on the nose face sized to fit between the headlight area.

For the lamp strip, I'm positioning a thin glowing cyan box along the sloped top edge of the hood, calculating the slope angle between the hood points to figure out the correct rotation so the strip sits flush against the surface.

Positioning headlight pods on the bumper corners around x ±1.15, y 1.12, z 3.88, with small lens glow boxes layered just in front for the glow effect.

Now I'm wiring up rods for tow hooks and bull-bar components, making sure each uses the body bone for proper attachment, and settling on a color palette that mostly relies on existing paint presets like panelled hull and armor finishes rather than introducing many new custom colors.

I'm also setting up helper functions for boxes and cylinders so parts attach to the body bone with consistent positioning and orientation, then starting on tank-shaped cylinder geometry with specific radius, length, and segment counts.

Writing helper functions...

Still building suspension and axle components...

Now I'm laying out the ladder frame rails with C-channel flanges, cross members between them, and an underbody plate centered along the chassis.

I'm also working through the fender flare details, adding chamfered slabs above each wheel well tilted slightly front and back to taper the flare shape smoothly.

That overlap is minor since the cab sits above with fenders beside it, and the flare extending to 1.55 stays clear of the cab's ±1.4 sides. I'm sketching SVG textures for the grille (dark slats with glyph details) and a hazard stripe pattern of yellow rects with black diagonals, while skipping the wheel arch liner and mud details as unnecessary.

Now I'm working out a "WARHOUND" text decal for the skirt panel, figuring out the orientation math so the text reads correctly for a viewer standing at +x looking toward -x — computing the right-vector via forward×up to confirm which direction the text should run along the skirt surface.

I'm also planning additional details within the part budget: a front skid plate, tow hooks, and a bull-bar with vertical rods and bars protruding from the front bumper area, placing them at specific coordinates beyond the main box geometry.

Now I'm moving to writing the actual construction code, importing the glow and clockwork kits for materials, setting up axle positions per side, and generating neon skirt strip segments with armor paneling along the body sides.

Adding neon trim details...

Now I'm thinking about the wheel well skirt segments near the bumper, deciding to skip that for simplicity, and planning out the plane and sweep geometry for the arch using arc parameters with center, start point, axis, and angle.

Adding more structural details...
